recipes.title: Chicken & Vegetable Stir-Fry
recipes.tagline: Fast, high-heat cooking: velveted chicken, crisp veg and a glossy pan sauce.
recipes.timeNote: Rice cooks alongside, so it doesn't add to the total.
recipes.servedWith: Served with rice (included in the numbers).

lines.text: 2 chicken breast fillets (about 320 g), sliced about 1 cm thick against the grain
1 onion, cut into wedges and separated into petals
1 head of broccoli (about 350 g), florets plus the sliced stalk
150 g chestnut mushrooms, sliced about 0.5 cm
150 g long-grain rice (75 g per person)

steps.title: Velvet the chicken
steps.body: Toss the sliced chicken with the cornflour and 1 tbsp soy, then leave it while you prep everything else. The thin coating shields the meat from the fierce heat, so it stays juicy.

steps.title: Prep everything first
steps.body: Cut all the veg and line it up in cooking order. Once the pan is hot this dish moves in minutes, with no time to chop. Slicing tip: 15–20 min in the freezer firms the chicken up for cleaner slices.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.body: About 20 minutes before you want to eat. Rinse the rice until the water runs fairly clear, then use about 270 ml water for 150 g rice. Bring to the boil, lid on, lowest heat for 10–12 min. Don't peek or stir. Rest 5–10 min off the heat, then fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.body: Stir together the soy, oyster sauce, honey, cornflour, water and garlic powder. The garlic powder goes in here rather than into the hot pan, where it would scorch.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.body: Heat 1 tbsp oil until hot but not screaming (ceramic pans don't like fierce heat). Add the chicken in a single layer and leave it to colour before turning. Cook until golden and just cooked through, then lift out.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.body: Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic, ginger and chilli. Stir for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Firm veg
steps.body: Add the broccoli and beans and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add a splash of water, cover to steam briefly, then uncover and let the water cook off.

steps.title: Medium veg
steps.body: Add the onion and mushrooms, with room to brown rather than steam.

steps.title: Courgette last
steps.body: It softens fast, so keep some bite.

steps.title: Combine
steps.body: Return the chicken. Stir the sauce (the cornflour sinks to the bottom) and pour it in. Toss for about a minute until glossy and thickened, then take off the heat and stir in the sesame oil.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Straight away, over the rice.

tips: Lower-salt swap: most of this dish's salt comes from the soy sauce. Tesco's reduced-salt soy is the same price.
Sesame oil is a finishing oil. It burns if you fry with it, so it goes in at the end.
Wood or silicone utensils only on the ceramic pan.
Leftover rice: cool it within about an hour, refrigerate, eat within 1–2 days, and reheat once until piping hot.
equipment: Saucepan with a lid for the rice

recipes.title: Chicken, Potato & Vegetable Traybake
recipes.tagline: Hands-off oven roasting, with the veg staged by density so everything finishes together.
recipes.timeNote: Add 20–30 min beforehand if you marinate the chicken.
recipes.servedWith: Potatoes are the carb, so no rice needed.
recipes.notes: First cook: the courgette went mushy, the chicken was a little dry, and it wasn't quite filling. Now fixed in the method: thick courgette added last, chicken out at 75°C, and potatoes to make it a full meal.

lines.text: 2 chicken breast fillets (about 320 g), butterflied to an even 1.5 cm, or cut into 3 cm chunks
2 baking potatoes (about 500 g), in 2.5 cm chunks
100 g green beans, trimmed and halved
150 g okra, whole or halved lengthways

steps.title: Marinate the chicken (optional)
steps.body: 20–30 min ahead: oil, lemon and salt, or a spoonful of natural yoghurt. A before-you-start job.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.body: 200°C fan (220°C conventional / gas 7), before you start chopping, so it's properly hot when the tray goes in.

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.body: Potatoes into 2.5 cm chunks (even size matters more than shape). Butterfly the chicken to an even 1.5 cm: hand flat on top, knife parallel to the board, open it like a book. Even thickness means even cooking.

steps.title: Potatoes in first
steps.body: Toss with 1 tbsp of the oil and a pinch of salt, and spread out with room. Roast about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Dense veg
steps.body: Toss the broccoli, beans, onion and okra in oil and seasoning, add to the tray and tuck in the garlic. Roast about 10 minutes.

steps.title: Chicken and mushrooms
steps.body: Oil and season them (paprika too, if using) and add to the tray. Roast about 5 minutes.

steps.title: Courgette last
steps.body: Thick-cut and with room, so it keeps some bite. Roast about 12 minutes more.

steps.title: Check the chicken
steps.body: As soon as the thickest part reads 75°C, take it out. Leaving it longer is what dries it out.

steps.title: Rest and finish
steps.body: Rest 5 minutes, squeeze over the lemon and serve.

tips: Don't crowd the tray: crowded veg steams instead of browning. A second tray is the fix.
Extra-crispy potatoes: par-boil 8–10 min, drain, let them steam-dry, then roast.
Okra: trim the stem cap, halve lengthways, and wipe rather than soak.
The 4 tbsp of oil is roughly a third of this dish's calories. That's fine (olive oil is a good fat); it just explains the number.
Very hungry? Add half a potato per portion.
equipment: Large oven tray (or two if it's packed)
Foil or baking paper (optional, for easier washing-up)

recipes.title: Chicken Thigh, Bacon & Vegetable Braise
recipes.tagline: Wet-heat cooking: browning, fond and deglazing, then a gentle covered simmer.
recipes.timeNote: Rice cooks during the braise, so it doesn't add to the total.
recipes.servedWith: Served with rice (included in the numbers).
recipes.notes: First cook: good overall, but a strong burnt taste. The fond went black before it was scraped up. Now fixed in the method: deglaze after browning the chicken (and the mushrooms if needed), medium heat, and colour cues over timers.

lines.text: 2 streaky bacon rashers, snipped into 1 cm strips
150 g white mushrooms, halved (quartered if wider than about 4 cm)
1 bird's eye chilli, finely chopped (fierce: use half, deseeded, if unsure)
150 g green beans, trimmed and halved
1 tsp dried thyme or mixed herbs
½ tsp salt (add late, taste first)
150 g long-grain rice (75 g per person)

steps.title: Prep everything first
steps.body: Cut all the veg. Trim large fat blobs off the thighs and pat them really dry: a wet surface can't brown, it just steams until the water has gone.

steps.title: Render the bacon
steps.body: Into a cold pan, then turn to medium. Starting cold melts the fat out slowly instead of burning the meat first. Lift out with a slotted spoon and leave the fat.

steps.title: Brown the chicken
steps.body: Season, then medium heat (not medium-high), 3–4 min a side, left completely alone. Colour only, not cooked through. Remove.

steps.title: Deglaze #1 — do not skip
steps.body: With the pan still hot, splash in about 50 ml of the stock and scrape the base immediately. Pour that liquid into a bowl and set it aside. The pan is now clean and the flavour is saved, which is what stops the fond burning during the later dry stages.

steps.title: Brown the mushrooms
steps.body: Cut face down, with room. They release water first and look wet; keep going until it has boiled off and they turn golden. Remove. If the base is darkening again, repeat the splash-and-scrape into the same bowl.

steps.title: Flavour base
steps.body: Medium heat, onion (and carrot if using) with a pinch of salt, until translucent and just catching gold. Salt draws moisture out and helps them soften rather than fry.

steps.title: Garlic and chilli
steps.body: Just until fragrant. Garlic burns fast and turns bitter.

steps.title: Liquid in
steps.body: Add the remaining stock plus the reserved deglazing liquid, the tomato purée, herbs and bay leaf, scraping the base once more. Tomato purée is sugary and scorches, so if the pan is hot, add it with the liquid rather than before it.

steps.title: Braise gently
steps.body: Return the chicken and its juices. The liquid should come roughly halfway up, not cover: that's the difference between a braise and a boil. Lazy, occasional bubbles only; lid on, lowest heat. About 15 minutes in, start the rice: rinse 150 g, about 270 ml water, boil, lid on, lowest heat 10–12 min, don't peek, then rest 5–10 min. If timing drifts, let the braise wait rather than the rice.

steps.title: Beans, mushrooms and bacon back in
steps.body: Lid on. Any longer and the beans go drab.

steps.title: Check, reduce, finish
steps.body: Thighs are safe at 75°C but nicer at 80–85°C. If the sauce is thin, lid off and bubble to reduce. Remove the bay leaf, taste, adjust salt and pepper, then add a squeeze of lemon: the acid snaps the rich, long-cooked flavours back into focus.

tips: Judge browning by colour, not the timer: deep chestnut brown is the target; black is burnt.
If the fond ever goes black, wipe the pan out with kitchen paper and carry on with fresh oil. Losing it costs far less than the bitterness does.
Salt late: the stock cube and bacon are already salty, so taste before adding the ½ tsp. You may not need it all.
Thicker sauce: toss the thighs in 1 tbsp plain flour before browning.
Never put okra in this dish. Wet, saucy cooking is exactly where it goes slimy.
Instead of rice: crusty bread, or 2 potatoes in 2.5 cm chunks added at the braising step.
equipment: Wide pan with a lid (foil pressed over the top works)
An uncoated or stainless pan, or a lidded casserole, gives better fond than ceramic non-stick

recipes.title: Beef, Bean & Lentil Chilli
recipes.tagline: Browned mince, bloomed spices and red lentils that melt into the sauce. Cook once, eat one, freeze three.
recipes.style: Hob · one pot · batch of 4 · freezes well
recipes.servedWith: Served with 100 g rice per portion (included in the numbers).

lines.text: 2 peppers (any colour), seeds and white pith removed, in 1.5 cm pieces
2 carrots, diced about 1 cm (small, so they soften in time)
1 bird's eye chilli, finely chopped (the heat)
100 g dried red split lentils, rinsed
2 × 400 g tins kidney beans, drained and rinsed
400 ml boiling water, for the stock
Salt only after tasting (up to ¼ tsp)
400 g rice (100 g per portion), cooked fresh each time

steps.title: Prep everything
steps.body: Chop the veg. Tip all four spices into one small bowl: they cook in under a minute, so there's no time to open jars later. Make the stock. Rinse the lentils in the sieve until the water runs mostly clear, and pick out any tiny stones. Drain and rinse the beans. Open the tomato tins.

steps.title: Brown the mince
steps.body:
Oil in the pot, then the mince. Press it into one flat layer and leave it alone for 4–5 min, then break it up with the spoon. Grey liquid will pool: that's water leaving the meat. Keep going until it boils away.

Ready when: the bubbling turns to a sizzle and the pieces are brown and crumbly.

steps.title: Veg in
steps.body:
Onion, carrot, pepper and a pinch of salt straight in with the mince. Their water lifts the brown bits off the base as they cook.

Ready when: the onion is soft and see-through.

If the base goes darker than chestnut brown: splash in about 50 ml of the stock and scrape.

steps.title: Garlic and chilli
steps.body: Stir until fragrant.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.body:
Heat down to medium-low, tip in the spice bowl and stir constantly. The flavour dissolves into the hot fat and loses its raw, dusty taste.

Ready when: it smells strongly fragrant and darkens slightly.

If it smells acrid or looks black: go straight to the next step. The liquid stops it instantly.

steps.title: Liquid in
steps.body: Tomatoes, tomato purée, stock, lentils and pepper, scraping the base. The purée goes in with the liquid because its sugar scorches in a dry pan. Bring to a bubble.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.body:
Lid ajar so water escapes and the sauce thickens. Low–medium, steady gentle bubbles. Stir every 5 min, scraping the bottom, because lentils sink and stick. If it gets very thick before the lentils soften, add about 100 ml water.

Ready when: the lentils have mostly melted into the sauce with no chalky bite.

Eating tonight? Start the rice now: 100 g rice to about 180 ml water.

steps.title: Beans in
steps.body:
They're already cooked, so they only need heating through. Adding them late keeps them whole.

Ready when: a spoon dragged across the base leaves a trail that stays open for a second.

steps.title: Taste and finish
steps.body: Taste before adding any salt: the stock cube is already salty. Squeeze in the lemon to lift the rich, long-cooked flavour.

tips: Medium heat unless a step says otherwise. Timers are guides; the cues win.
Tesco's 20% fat mince (£3.25 for 500 g) makes it about 45p a portion cheaper, with about 20 g more fat and 8.5 g more saturates per portion, less whatever you spoon off.
Lower salt: use a reduced-salt stock cube or skip the final salt.
More energy: more rice (25 g extra adds about 90 kcal), 30 g grated cheddar (about +125 kcal and +7 g protein) or a tortilla wrap.
equipment: A pot of at least 4 litres, with a lid. It makes about 3 litres. If yours is smaller, brown the mince in a frying pan, then move everything into your biggest saucepan.
Sieve or colander, wooden spoon, small bowl for the spices, jug for the stock.
4 freezer containers of about 750 ml, plus tape and a pen for labels.
storage: Cool fast. Portion straight into containers, lids off until the steam stops, then freeze within 2 hours. Never put the whole hot pot in the fridge.
Leave a 1–2 cm gap at the top: liquid expands as it freezes.
Label with the name and date. Best within about 3 months.
Freeze the chilli, not the rice. Cook rice fresh; it's the risky one to reheat.
Defrost in the fridge overnight and eat within 24 hours.
Reheat until piping hot and steaming all the way through. In the microwave, stir halfway to kill cold spots. Reheat once, never refreeze.
Mince bought frozen? Defrost it, cook it, then freeze the chilli. Never refreeze raw meat that has been defrosted.
